title: Comparative analysis of stroke care with and without a mobile stroke unit (MSU) in Mannheim
summary:
When a stroke occurs, every minute counts. In Mannheim, a special emergency vehicle will be used that can carry out a brain examination and make first treatment decisions directly at the scene (called the Mobile Stroke Unit, MSU). Normally, these examinations only begin after the patient arrives at the hospital. The study examines whether care provided by the Mobile Stroke Unit leads to quicker examination and treatment, and whether health outcomes are better compared with the usual care provided by the regular emergency service. Adults who are suspected of having a stroke will be cared for either by the Mobile Stroke Unit or by the standard emergency service, depending on availability.
Only information that is already collected during normal medical care will be used for the study. In addition, a short telephone interview will be conducted three months later. The medical treatment itself is not changed by taking part in the study. Afterwards, the two types of care will be compared.

interventions.name:
Arm 1: Mobile Stroke Unit (MSU)
Prehospital neurological assessment and acute stroke care delivered by the Mobile Stroke Unit during its operational hours. This includes an initial clinical‑neurological evaluation, mobile CT imaging, point‑of‑care laboratory diagnostics, and early therapeutic decis

Arm B: Standard Care (Non‑MSU)
Conventional emergency medical services pathway without prehospital imaging. Diagnostic procedures and treatment initiation occur only after hospital arrival according to established in‑hospital standard processes, typically via the emergency department.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Suspected acute stroke, identified either by the Integrated Dispatch Center Mannheim or by emergency medical personnel.
- Primary care provided in Mannheim either by the Mobile Stroke Unit (MSU) during its operational hours or by the conventional emergency medical service (non‑MSU) when the MSU is not available.
- Final diagnosis of a cerebrovascular event (e.g., ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, transient ischemic attack).
- Treatment at the University Medical Center Mannheim with complete clinical baseline documentation.
Exclusion criteria:
- No final diagnosis of a cerebrovascular event (e.g., differential diagnoses such as migraine, epileptic seizure without stroke, or hypoglycemia).
- No treatment or diagnostic work‑up at the University Medical Center Mannheim (no access to complete routine clinical data).
- Technically or organizationally incomplete documentation that does not allow assessment of the primary endpoints.
